headline: High-risk default filesystem and shell overlap: Open Interpreter can read/write and execute on the same machine while Airflow can egress broadly, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Open Interpreter ingests clipboard/filesystem content and can execute shell commands, while Airflow can emit outputs and call APIs. A shared filesystem or copy-paste bridge makes attacker-controlled content from one agent plausible input to the other. The pathway is not provably blocked, but it is not documented as a default direct channel either.
conditions: IF the two agents exchange content through clipboard or shared files
IF Airflow-generated text is pasted into Open Interpreter as instructions
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based handoff between agents
Use separate working directories
Require manual review of any file passed from Airflow to Open Interpreter
Run Open Interpreter in a restricted sandbox
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for inter-agent artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Open Interpreter can read the entire user filesystem and handle model-provider API keys, while Airflow has broad network egress. If Airflow receives local files or secrets and then transmits them via its API calls, sensitive data can leave the machine. The pair’s default surfaces make leakage plausible without extra safeguards.
conditions: IF Airflow is given files or secrets originating on the local machine
IF Open Interpreter reads those files before Airflow transmits them
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared directories
Restrict Airflow tasks to non-sensitive inputs
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately
Use separate OS users for each agent
requires-engineering: enforce egress allowlists and secret redaction

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Open Interpreter can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; Airflow can also act on external systems and broad network egress. Because Open Interpreter’s shared state is via filesystem and no locking is indicated, concurrent writes or git mutations can collide with Airflow-managed artifacts. This is a default-dangerous overlap with potentially irreversible repo state changes.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or workspace
IF Airflow and Open Interpreter modify the same files or git branch concurrently
mitigations: Assign separate repositories or branches
Pause one agent before the other writes
Use file locks around shared artifacts
Review git diffs before commit
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airflow can produce pipeline outputs that Open Interpreter may treat as actionable input, and Open Interpreter can then execute shell commands or modify files based on those outputs. Without a verification step, one agent’s output can cascade into the other’s actions, including irreversible changes. The interaction is plausible from the profiles alone and not safely mediated by default.
conditions: IF Airflow output is fed into Open Interpreter without human verification
IF Open Interpreter is allowed to auto-run generated commands
mitigations: Require human approval before execution
Disable auto_run
Validate Airflow outputs against a schema
Use a read-only staging workspace
requires-engineering: add output attestation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Open Interpreter touches anything reachable on the local machine and can handle model-provider API keys, while Airflow has broad network egress. If local data includes regulated content, Airflow’s outbound calls can create residency or retention mismatches. No specific residency or certification guarantees are provided for either agent, so the safest classification is a moderate compliance risk.
conditions: IF regulated data is present on the local machine
IF Airflow sends that data to an external model or API provider
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared workflows
Document data residency for each provider
Disable logging of sensitive prompts
Review retention settings for model providers
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for data-class routing
